hook.line: Canada's flicking game: flick discs in from the edge of a round board — the nearer the middle, the more they score. The hole in the centre is 20.
hook.say: Let me show you a game born in Canadian parlours!

ch.say: The oldest board was a birthday present!
p: Crokinole is a Canadian disc-flicking game played on a round board. Its name is generally said to come from the French-Canadian word croquignole, a flick of the finger.
The earliest known board was made in 1876 in Perth County, Ontario, by Eckhardt Wettlaufer for his son's fifth birthday. It is kept at the Joseph Schneider Haus in Kitchener.

ch.t: A round board and eight pegs
ch.cap: A crokinole board: the 5, 10 and 15 circles, eight pegs on the 15 circle, the 20 hole in the middle
p: The playing surface is a round board 66 cm (26 in) across, divided by circles of 20, 41 and 61 cm: the further in, the more a disc scores. Eight pegs — posts with rubber sleeves — stand on the 15 circle, and a shallow 3.5 cm hole sits in the middle.
A ditch runs round the edge to catch the discs that fly off. The discs are wooden, about 3.2 cm across. Boric acid powder was once used for speed; today players use starch spray or wax.
